title: THE ART OF WAR - RULES OF ENGAGEMENT

sense.text:
“As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.” Just like cold water when you have travelled a far distance through a desert. That good news from a far country is this truth carried to our people in the far places of the earth.

A lot of our people in America take this truth for granted, because America nourishes us, gives us comfort and fills all our necessities. Go out to these other countries and our people feel the oppression. They feel the iron fist, the depression, the oppression, the suppression, more than us, and they are a lot more receptive when they hear this truth. It comes to them like a fresh glass of cold water.

That is what was found in Papua New Guinea: a 30-hour trip there and 30 hours back, and it was all worth it. It is no vacation. It is continual, constant work in a short time. Of every country travelled to, there is no place on earth like Papua New Guinea, where the people are so receptive and their biblical intelligence is on another level. The whole of Revelation 13 was broken down on the street and they understood it. They are so studious that the brothers run out of topics: they sit for three and four hours, and then they follow you to your car. The truth went out on the biggest radio and news station in the country, and the host said he would take the consequences, because the truth is the truth and it is in the Bible.

The Lord even shut down a stage before thousands of people, and then a promised hall, so that the brothers would go to the university campus. There one young man answered every question. He had been watching and studying IUIC for years, his notebook full of notes, not knowing the brothers were on the island. He came to the Sabbath and was casting down lies, killing John 3:16 and the Gentile question with the precepts. The Lord orchestrated the whole trip for one soul, to recover that one sheep. So never think the work you do is insignificant because you see one spirit. Instead of letting human emotions get the best of you, read into the spirit and see what the Lord is doing. Think of the 144,000: it takes one to bring the end of this world.

precepts.why:
“For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off. It is not in heaven, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it unto us”.

“Neither is it beyond the sea, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it unto us, that we may hear it, and do it?” Isaiah 11:11 calls the place where our people are scattered the islands of the sea. Our people over the sea don't have the word, so they ask: who shall go over the sea for us and bring this word of God to us, that we may hear it?

The Lord commissioned IUIC to go over the seas and bring it to our people, so that they may hear this word and identify: I am a part of the tribes. I am somebody. I am not a kanaka, nor any of the derogatory words they put on us.

That is why the brothers are told: get your passports, get your finances and your affairs together, and travel and help spread this gospel. Captains have gone to the Dominican Republic and Papua New Guinea, but a few cannot do it on their own.

sense.text:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people”. The root of Jesse is Jesus Christ. The ensign for the people means Christ will stand as a sign for the people.

“to it shall the Gentiles seek”: to Christ and his Bible the people called Gentiles shall seek. “and his rest shall be glorious”: our rest in the kingdom will be glorious.

Verse 10 says the Gentiles shall seek it, and verse 11 says the remnant of his people. The Gentiles in verse 10 are the remnant of his people in verse 11.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. The first time was when God allowed Moses to deliver us out of Egypt. The second time is when Christ delivers us out of Egypt, which is America.

Then he gives the geographical locations where his people will be in the last days, before his second return. “from Assyria”: Assyria is modern-day Turkey, where there is a remnant of Israel called the Afro-Turks. “and from Egypt”: a remnant in Egypt, northeast Africa. “and from Pathros”: a remnant in Sudan. “and from Cush”: a remnant in Ethiopia. “and from Elam”: a remnant in India, Pakistan and Iran, called the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits. “and from Shinar”: a remnant in Iraq, the Afro-Iraqis. “and from Hamath”: a remnant in Syria, the Afro-Syrians.

“and from the islands of the sea”: a remnant of our people, our brothers and sisters, in the South Pacific, the South Sea Islands. That is why we go to these locations.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations”: the ensign is Christ, the Bible. “and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel”, because the remnant of his people scattered through these locations was cast out of the land. “and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Israel is scattered to the four corners of the earth, so those Gentiles in verse 10 are Israel.

The Maori people of New Zealand listen intently to the brothers on the live show and say: we identify with you, we identify with the curses, we live in the same conditions. A sister told the brothers that her people formed their Black Panther Party after ours. You have to be able to identify and follow the spirit when it comes to locating the tribes.

“Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion”. In the 1960s Judah stooped down and couched as a lion: Judah was about to attack the system. They formed political and civil rights groups like the Black Panther Party and the Black Power Movement, with activists like Stokely Carmichael, Fred Hampton, Martin Luther King, Bunchy Carter, Malcolm X and Medgar Evers fighting against oppression.

Little do you know, when Judah formed the Black Panther Party, Judah ignited the spirit in all the other tribes. That is Ezekiel 37, the valley of dry bones coming to life. When Judah woke up and fought oppression, the spirit of God first entered the earth for us to stand up as a nation. Then you had the Brown Berets, Issachar rising up; the Young Lords, Ephraim; AIM, the American Indians.

And not only in America. When Judah rose up to speak, Judah activated the tribes globally. There were the Papua New Guinea Black Panthers, the Dalit Panthers rose up in India, and the Maori formed a Panther party at the same time. The spirit of Judah activated the whole planet. Don't tell me this Bible ain't spiritual.

“Naphtali is a hind let loose”: let loose from captivity. In the time of the Persians, around 538 BC, King Cyrus gave the northern kingdom of Israel liberty, either to stay or to go back to the land and build, and some of them decided to leave.

“he giveth goodly words”: those are peaceable words. Pacific means peace, a peaceable place. The geographical location is identified by the title given to it: Naphtali will live where the place is called the Pacific, the place of peace.

These are the Maori people, always fighting against the system. Every nation and culture has one group that stands out, and they stand out: their haka, the sister who ripped up the document, and when an LGBT parade came to New Zealand they went into the street and shut it down, saying we ain't allowing that in our community. They don't look like our people to some, but what did our people look like before we came to the truth? The tattoos and such are traditions adopted when we mingled amongst the heathen.

Esau's missionaries write that there are traces of the Israelites among them, but that it is not conclusive or scientifically proven. Yet the spirit says, my sheep hear my voice, I know them, and they follow me: they are keeping the commandments, pouring in and listening. The counsel came to check out the migration, and at two in the morning the spirit led to a book from 1926 that laid out the whole route of the northern kingdom's migration and every country it touched.

precepts.why:
“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.” The northern kingdom was exiled and deported out of the nation of Israel into Assyria. That was the first major captivity, when the northern kingdom started taking on Gentile titles and customs.

Then the history jumps to when King Cyrus gave us liberty: Naphtali, the hind let loose. “But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” They said: let's leave this part of the world and go to the western hemisphere, the round world, the Americas.

The book Origin and Migration of the New Zealand Maori shows the route. European and American scientists call it a controversy, but they don't dictate our history, our traditions, our customs or our culture; stand back in the corner and wait for your destruction, because it's coming. The Maori is clear about the history of his own race; he doesn't need their science or their archaeology.

Their legends say the land where mankind was created was Assyria. Not Jerusalem, because Assyria is where the northern kingdom was officially turned into Gentiles and lost all trace and recollection of where they came from. That was the first valley of the shadow of death, where their nationality was wiped away. That is why Ephraim was broken, that it be not a people: it happened in Assyria.

They say there were twelve nations, or houses, all descended from Hakopa, Jacob. They first migrated to Egypt, where they built cities; returned to Assyria, the Assyrian captivity; then split into two parties, the southern and northern kingdoms. Ten crossed the Caucasus (there were Israelites in the Caucasus Mountains who taught the Khazarians, Esau, Judaism) and journeyed across Europe to Portugal, some dropping off along the way. Five nations sailed from Portugal to Mexico: the Israelites settled in Mexico, and the serpent nation is why the Mexicans worship Quetzalcoatl, the serpent god. When Mexico fell they scattered to the Yucatan, Central America, Jamaica and Guiana, the Arawak. Those left went south to Peru, a new and uninhabited land, where never mankind dwelt.

Then one nation, the Arawa, went still further west to Easter Island, through the South Sea Islands, Melanesia, from melanin, the islands of black people, and reached New Zealand. Their traditional descent is from Isaac, son of Abraham, and from Jacob came the twelve houses, Israel, which they call the people of the son god. They went into idolatry, carrying the crests of the turtle and the rest, that Assyrian garbage the northern kingdom took with them, but they kept the tradition that they came from Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Not all ten tribes came west: the northern kingdom was scattered all throughout, some to China and Japan, some to India, and some of the northern tribes were dropped off around Africa, in Morocco, Nigeria and Madagascar.

“And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, satisfied with favour, and full with the blessing of the Lord”. Naphtali will be satisfied with favour and full of blessings: mineral rights, gold, silver, copper, crude oil, palladium and platinum, an abundance of forestry (all the other nations go to Papua New Guinea for their wood), and fishery.

“possess thou the west and the south.” The Maori pushed down to the South Sea Islands. The southwest Pacific includes Australia and New Zealand, where the Maori reside, and the islands of Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia: Papua New Guinea, Fiji, the Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and New Caledonia. The southwest Pacific is where the tribe of Naphtali would inhabit, and now there is the documented history of the exact route from ancient Assyria.

sense.text:
An ancient general wrote down the rules of war, and the rules have not changed. Every war is fought twice, once on the battlefield and once in the mind before it begins. If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear a hundred battles. You know your enemy, sin. But do you know yourself, where you are weak, what opens the gate? Every soldier is given rules of engagement before the battle, because the man who waits until the enemy is in front of him to make a plan has already lost. Know your triggers, know the enemy, know yourself.

“Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” In this truth there will be constant battles in the mind, continual strife and engagement. The battles are spiritual, and this warfare starts primarily within our mind.

People come to this truth thinking that as soon as they find out they are Israel, the red carpet will be laid out for them into the kingdom. No: as soon as you find out you are Israel, your true battle and warfare begins. Like in The Matrix, once you unplug, the sentinels and the agents, Mr. Smith, come after you. There is a spirit on you that gives off an aura that attracts demons, because they are trying to bring you back into the matrix. That is why Paul says to endure hardness.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. We are at war, so don't involve yourself in the affairs of this life: don't entangle yourself with the political affairs or the religious affairs. Like The Book of Eli, he could not leave his path even when he saw a woman being taken advantage of. God has placed each of us on a path toward a destination, with a purpose, and there are distractions and routes that would take us off our journey.

“that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” God chose us to be soldiers. This is not a Christian church where you come for a feel-good sermon of prosperity, take notes every Sabbath, go home and do nothing with it. Everybody that walks in the door enlists in God's army and will be deployed, because this is warfare: not physical, but a spiritual war.

precepts.why:
“For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.” We have to change our mind. Every second, minute and hour of every day there is a continual, constant war, and by wise counsel we make our war.

That is why there is the accountability list, brothers accountable for other brothers: the members, soldiers, officers and sisters are all at war. But war with what? Some come in oblivious to what is happening, and that is why we keep losing: you don't know you are in a battle.

The first step to being successful is to understand that you are in a war, whether you can see it or not. Open your eyes to the intricate details and nuances: the small voices you hear in your head, the little seeds dropped in you, the little speeches. Everything around you is at war with you. Ask a brother how his week was and he says, It's the battle. That's all you need to know: you're still here for today.

sense.text: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the scriptures and you shall not fulfil the lust that is within our flesh.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit”: the flesh is against the spirit of God within us, against our ability to do right. “and the Spirit against the flesh”: the spirit of God, the laws and commandments that are supposed to be ingrained in our minds, is against our fleshly temptations. Whatever the body craves (the cake, the smell of food, the candy, the woman, the alcohol, the drug addiction), the scriptures and the spirit of God within us say no, don't do that. It is a constant battle inside.

“and these are contrary the one to the other”: they are warring against each other. It is a natural desire within us to give in to our sin, because this body was fashioned in a sinful nature. Everybody fashioned after Adam was born in a sinful body, and this body is our test from day one.

So when a brother is asked how his week was and says it was good, nothing happened, he is not honest. If we are struggling and fighting to keep our head above water and you have it all figured out, you must be better than Adam, an angel without sin, better than Christ, than David, than Solomon, stronger than Samson. Which of the prophets are you above?

This is a spiritual warfare. “Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.” That is what we tell our brothers: be strong when you go out in these streets, and when you go home, be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might.

“Put on the whole armour of God”: the whole armour, because you are going to be tested and tried from angles you don't even know. While you are fighting on the front end, the enemy is pursuing you from the back. While you protect your back, he comes from the side, from the left, and while you defend every angle another enemy is infiltrating your thought process.

We are fighting an enemy with thousands upon thousands of years of practice in warfare against the very best of us, from the first person on this earth, and an enemy we can't even see. That's a scary thing. You have to tap into the spirit to see him. And seeing him doesn't mean you can block the punch: you might see Mike Tyson's punch, but no matter how you put that arm up, you still get knocked out.

“that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” That's the point.

“Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts”. Darts are shot at you continually from every angle, and we have to gear ourselves up in a spiritual warfare to shield ourselves and quench them all.

This art of war is not about fighting or about teaching. It is the intricate details we have to address in the day-to-day fight in order to survive this truth, identifying them and engaging in tactical warfare.

To war a good warfare, a warrior must be experienced in the art of battle, and you cannot gain experience if you have never fought. Some of you have been sheltered all your life, or gave in to your sins all your life. Some of you never got hit: you might know who the enemy is and where it's coming from, but can you take the hit, the fiery thoughts, when they come?

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations”. You may be going through it financially, with your wife or husband, at your job, in every angle of life. Glory in tribulation, because you have to be forged into pure gold, the diamond in the rough. Pressure can break you or it can form, fashion and shape you; to grow properly you have to be put in the fire of adversity. Trials are good; pain is good for growth. Everybody wants to be great, but nobody wants to go through what great people go through. David didn't just become David. The mighty men went into the forest with David and were formed in adversity, and that is why their names live to this generation.

“knowing that tribulation worketh patience”. In your patience you possess your soul. What is God trying to teach me? Some go a long time without a job because they still haven't learned the lesson; they are not paying attention to its details. If you don't identify the test you might destroy yourself with the blessing of the next level. Some can't travel because the Lord hasn't blessed the finances, because they are not at that level yet. He keeps you there until you identify the test and grow from it, and then he blesses you and brings you up.

“And patience, experience”: in your patience, going through your trials, you identify why you are going through it. It's tactical warfare: you are getting hit from every angle, you block, you learn, you see. People wonder how the bishop, the deacons and the captains speak the way they do, as if they read your mind. No: they experienced it so many times it became natural. That experience, gained through trials, battles and adversity, is what lets you counsel, guide, teach and relate. Captain Young in the prison ministry can speak to people on a different level because he engaged in a different warfare, in the streets, in prison and in this truth.

“and experience, hope”: you have confidence now. You've been through the trials and gained experience, and you know this is the truth. You've seen what the Lord can do; you can see the spirit guiding you; you gain discernment into the spiritual realm, because your eyes were opened.

precepts.why:
“For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.” That is warfare. For Christ to be a successful high priest, able to judge matters and guide and instruct people, he had to be tempted in all areas.

You might say, Lord, why am I going through this? So that you can be of benefit to others going through the same things. Your trial might be worse than other people's. Why don't they battle what I battle? Because there are people out in the world, not yet brought in, who battle things on a higher level, and the Lord has to bring you through it psychologically. He shows you the thought process of sin and its intricate details, the things people can't see: why it happened, how, when, the time frame, the situation, the scenario.

He shows you every aspect of the battle and all that comes behind that sin, so that you can be a faithful high priest and teach and deal with people who are dealing with these things on another level.

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” When you get to that point of warfare, the experience you gain lets you discern both good and evil. You can see the battle. You can see the punches and the knockout coming. You can see Satan for what he is and where he's coming from.

sense.text:
Why do we need rules of engagement? Who is the enemy? Don't let the Christians fool you: they say the enemy is Satan. Yes, the enemy is Satan, and the enemy is the white man; the white man's the devil, always keep that in mind. But here we are dealing with a different level of warfare.

“Be sober, be vigilant”: be clear-minded, alert and watchful. “because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. There is no predator worse or more capable than a lion. A lion hunts in the dark; it hunts when it's noisy, and most of all when it's raining, so it can cover its tracks. Sometimes you can't see it or hear it. Satan is that roaring lion who covers his tracks, hunts in the silence and in the noise, spots you, picks you out and devours you. That is the enemy we are dealing with: an enemy you can't see.

“Whom resist stedfast in the faith”. Satan, the roaring lion, is the enemy identified. So the rules of engagement are the rules we develop in order to engage in spiritual tactical warfare.

The commandments are the rules of engagement. But because of the augmentation of modern society, the commandments have to be broken down to answer the technological advances, the nuances of sin and the evolution of society. Know the battle, the enemy and your weaknesses, and write it down.

“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith”. There are levels to examination. You say, I battle this, I battle that. Go deeper: why do you battle it? When did the battle start? When does it happen, what time of the day? There's a time, an hour, a day; there's a pattern to the battle, to your sin, to when you give in, to why you react a certain way and why it keeps coming around at the same time. All these things are patterns: traceable and identifiable.

“prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you”. The spirit of Christ is supposed to give you the spirit to know yourself; if you have the spirit of Christ you are supposed to have a high level of discernment.

“except ye be reprobates?” Except you are reprobate: constantly giving in and not even fighting. That is the only reason you won't know yourself, the only reason you say I'm good every week. You're not really in the fight. You're the same person you were when you came in, and you never fought or even cared to address the problems.

precepts.why:
“Search me, O God, and know my heart”. You might not know yourself. Lord, there are levels of me I don't know: I keep doing the same things, getting the same results, not growing. So David says, search me, take me to the next level, know what is within me.

“try me”. That's scary. Some of you want to be great, want to be leaders: this is the prayer you have to make, and if you ask for it, expect the results. The Lord says: you want strength, I'll give you problems; you want wisdom, I'll put you in bad situations. Why are you always arguing? So you can be a great teacher. Why are your kids so bad? So you learn to reach kids on another level. Why do I have this kind of wife? Because if you can set her in order, organize her thoughts and bring her to a level of godliness, you can set the nation in order. Some brothers' wives are quiet and easy; some are difficult, because the Lord has a path for that brother. A brother who can set a difficult sister in order might be an Abraham.

“and know my thoughts”. Some thoughts you can't even tell are good or wrong. Thoughts are not random; a spirit passes thoughts through you. The thought you call random was tactical and intentional, a seed the enemy planted for a week from now, a year, two years, five years, setting you up for the long run. Two years later you're in a sin and ask, how did I get into this? There was a time, a place, an hour and a day that thought was placed in you. That was Satan, setting up your fall, if you don't pay attention to it.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” That is our prayer.

sense.text: “What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?” What is man, that God should set his heart upon him?

“And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?” Every morning you are visited, and every moment of the day you are being tried whether you know it or not. Everything is a test. Sometimes you say, man, it's a good day. No, it's not: you just failed to see the test.

A real warrior always has his head on a swivel and is always prepared for the test. It's too quiet today; where's the setup? She's happy, I'm waiting for it. The kids are quiet; something's going on.

“How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?” Job says, what's so special about me? Is there somebody else you could test? Can you visit that brother over there who's been chilling? Can I get a break, some time to breathe? I don't even get a minute to swallow my spit before the next trial: tested here, tested there.

You make it through the day and say, I made it to my bed, the coast is clear. Then Satan visits your dreams: Nigga, you don't know who I am. I got you in the day and I got you in the night, like Freddy Krueger. God damn, Satan, in my dreams? Who am I, why am I so important? Can you bother somebody else? What about the other nations?

“I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?” You become a burden to yourself. Every day you wake up and say, here I go again: I keep failing, I keep falling, I keep doing this and that, I can't get right. Some of you fall away because of that burden.

precepts.why:
“Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long.” Be in the fear of God all the day long, because every moment you are being tried in this constant, continual warfare. From the second to the minute to the hour to the day you are at war, whether you know it or not, whether you like it or not. All it takes is one decision to shape your reality and your future.

A good exercise is your own personal rules of engagement, rules not to break concerning yourself and your triggers. They can deal in intricate detail with lust, with how you respond to people negatively, your anger triggers, your marital issues, whatever acknowledged flaw of character you want to change. Write them down every day, programming your rules into your vessel.

sense.text: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.”

“Bind them upon thy fingers”: bind God's commandments upon your fingers. “write them upon the table of thine heart”: there's a reason God says to write the laws on the table of your heart, your mind.

When you write things down and look at what you wrote, you are actually programming your mind, your vessel. Keep a journal. You can program an outcome you want to see, a characteristic you want to develop, a personality you want to come to pass. Write the commandments; write your outcome; write your progress.

The Bible speaks of writing the commandments down, and we have to write down the things we discuss, because we forget everything: car keys, wallet, even our children's names. That's how the mind is by design. We don't grow in self-examination because we don't know what we need to grow from. We have so many flaws of character and personality that are not progressive, and we don't progress because we don't write them down, keep them before us and meditate on them. Somebody tells you about yourself, the next day you forget, and five or ten years later you're the same nasty person: argumentative, short-tempered, soon angry. You know it and want to change it, but you keep forgetting it.

Our vessel alone is void of information unless we program it. Like a computer programmer writing code into the software so it functions the way he intends, write your code every morning: your ten commandments of rules not to break concerning yourself and your discipline, and rules to keep from day to day.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer”. A hearer hears: thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal, don't be so angry; an evil eye, lust, lasciviousness, looking on a maid to lust after her, malice, strife, contention, preeminence. You hear the word, you hear your problems, you receive correction, but you don't apply it, don't apply the commandments to your issues.

“he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass”. Your natural face is your sinful face. When you wake up and look in the mirror you see all your deficiencies: an eye booger, a pimple, hair not combed. On the carnal level, before you leave the house you clean yourself up: comb your beard, brush your teeth, wash your face, pop the pimple; sisters, a little makeup and a touch here and there. The glass is the Bible. Every day you come to the Bible with your natural, sinful face, and you are supposed to look in it and correct yourself, clean the sin within you, purify and sanctify your thoughts.

“For he beholdeth himself”: you see your flaws of character and personality, you hear your problems, you receive correction and counsel, you read about yourself and hear yourself in the class. “and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” You forget the correction, you forget your flaws, you forget what that sister told you to change. You forget what kind of person you were.

precepts.why:
“Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing”. The verse speaks of something else, but put it in writing. When you receive correction, when you identify a trait that is against what you want to be, write it down.

The bishop once corrected a brother in the war room and said, remember what I corrected you about three years ago? The bishop remembered the exact correction; the brother didn't, and he was still doing the same thing. He never grew from it, because he forgot what the correction was, and he is the same individual.

So write it all down, because you will forget: your flaws, your problems, everything you are that you don't want to be, the correction. Document it all, so you know what rules to put in place to gauge it when it approaches you, and meditate on it when it comes.

Brothers point out something you always do. Two brothers kept doing the same thing to me, and I thought, why do they keep messing with me? They had nothing against me: there was a flaw I kept repeating. So I had to write it down, program the outcome I wanted, map out what to correct and how, and put it into practice, until they said, you don't say anything anymore. I trained myself not to react, because I understood what they were trying to teach me about myself. Write it into existence, practice it, and it becomes your growth. That's leveling up.

“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way”: to know yourself. “but the folly of fools is deceit.”

A boxer gets hit with the right, gets hit with the left, drops his arm. How does he know? He studies himself on video: you're dropping your arm, keep your hands up, your jab is too short, extend. Spiritually it's the same: you are in a spiritual tactical warfare and have to learn how to fight. Study what got you knocked out last time: what the steps looked like, how, why and when you got hit. Document the steps. You may get hit ten more times, but with continual practice and observation you learn to block it and see it before it comes: it's going to happen at this time, this day, this hour, because you studied the tactics behind the approach.

sense.text:
How to engage in tactical warfare when it comes to lust. Lust is one of the biggest sins within a nation because it deals with procreation, be fruitful and multiply. It deals with your body and with human existence, so it is always going to be one of the biggest sins.

“abstain from fleshly lusts”. There are different lusts: lust of the flesh in pornography and prostitution, alcoholism, cigarettes. Everybody has some form of lust; it isn't just one direction.

“which war against the soul”. Our lust wars against our soul; it manipulates and alters our thought process. That's the point: it is a spiritual warfare.

Being taught this doesn't mean we all know how to overcome it; it's a battle each of us has to figure out. You can know the war and still get hit.

“whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” When you look on a woman to lust after her, you commit adultery in your mind. The thought comes before the act.

Here is the tactical approach to engaging with lust. “if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out”. Your right eye is not literally your eye. If something is offending you, remove that problem from your life. Don't engage it, don't entertain it, don't put it before you, don't be in the same room with it. You have to be intentional in approaching your lust, whatever it is.

“and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.” You may think you need something. If it keeps you from the intended result, from forward progress, keeps you in the same predicament, cast it far away. I don't care if you think you need it or it's an important part of your life. Know yourself and your triggers, because it is profitable that your whole body not be destroyed when Christ returns.

Rules of engagement for lust: from many observations, everybody falls into this sin the same way. One rule: no phone in bed or near you. People fall in their comfort, when they let their guard down and forget they're in a fight: in bed at night, relaxed, scrolling as a reward. But is it always you that's scrolling? The phone is an extension of you, and demonic activity is able to channel itself through these technologies and engage with us. It is the spirit within you scrolling for hours until it finds its target, the one video that triggers the lust within you, and then you engage in your sin. The demon you don't even know you battle finds what he's looking for, and you feed him.

So if you're serious: only a book or the Bible in bed. Cut off the internet and the technology, and commune with the Lord before you sleep, because that's Satan's time to attack you in your bed. Use devices for educational purposes; if it's that bad, remove the scrolling apps; make it purposeful and put a time limit on it. For some the trigger is drinking: they drink, let down their guard and give in to lust.

When you are weakened and give in, look back: what were the triggers, how were you set up, what defenses were taken down, how did you compromise your own defenses, who infiltrated them, and when? Did you break your own rules and let the enemy in? Never allow circumstances to break your rules, whatever the environment, timing or emotional feeling. These things seem harmless, but they leave just enough space for Satan to take control of your vessel. Knowing the battle and the enemy is one part; the biggest part is not compromising your defense system for anything. Discipline works at all times.

Your phone is part of your mind. Before phones, you remembered numbers yourself, kept photos in an album and in your memory; now the phone holds your numbers, photos, tasks and ideas. It has become an extension of your cognitive functions. It is part of you; you've become a cyborg. Leave the house without it and you know right away, because there's a spirit connecting it. Nikola Tesla was a prophet on the left side, in Esau's world: he tapped into radio frequencies with what was called the spirit radio and communicated with demons in the unseen world, and after it came the spirit phone. The phone was created as an extension of us into the unseen world, and whatever spirits are within us are attached to it. When someone manipulates your social media feed, they're manipulating part of your actual thinking: a thought you think is yours was steered into their direction. So have rules of engagement even for your phone, to protect your mind.

precepts.why:
“Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” The good manners are what you learn in this Bible. The evil communications are things like these digital devices that we give ourselves to, until you pick up your phone and ask, why did I pick it up? It's a gravitational pull; you can't help it. You scroll, and two hours later you don't know why you scrolled for two hours.

It leads you back to the same person you were, because the demonic spirit in your members is looking for it, and the spirit connected to the device channels it: aha, boom, got you, right back to the same person. That is how deep the battle is.

So have rules for engaging the phone and the computer. No scrolling; if I scroll, I do it intentionally, because I have a topic, a class to teach, a subject to study, and I do it safely, with a time limit and boundaries. Scroll without intention and it will manipulate you and bring you somewhere you don't want to go.

The phone, the TV, the iPad, the computer used to be in the living room or the study room. Now they're in your bedroom, because that's where you let go your defenses. Going to the TV was intentional; in bed you read a book or your scriptures and went to sleep. Put the TV in the room and you don't read; you watch and fall asleep, and the white man, the devil, the enemy, puts thoughts in your mind to keep you from progressing, from learning wisdom and moving forward. They took the phone off the wall and put it in the palm of your hand in your room. This is war: they brought the battle to your room.

“Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still.” David communed with the Lord in his bed, and they took that out and distracted you.

Commune with your own mind upon your bed: that's when you communicate with the Lord and study, right before you go to sleep, because it fashions your dreams and your thought process. You program your heart before you enter the spiritual realm. Either you program your mind or the enemy will program it on your phone as you scroll yourself to sleep. Why do you have nightmares? The spirit in what you were watching entered your spirit and your dreams.

Go to sleep with the Bible app or a class on, and you hear the scriptures in your dreams; the one teaching is in your dream carrying out the teaching, because you let the spirit in as you communed. That's how you affect your thoughts and dreams and shape your mind for the next day's battle. That's when you strengthen and refuel yourself.

sense.text:
Marriage, and tactical engagement in arguments with a spouse. There are many rules of engagement. You have to know your own battles, your triggers, your personality deficiencies and flaws of character, and write them down. Understand how the enemy will use them, and when, and at what time. Be detailed and observant: write down when it happens and you'll see a pattern, the same time, the same day, this person always does this at this hour. Then when it comes you know, and you've already put a plan of action in place for how to deal with that enemy when he comes for you. That's how detailed we have to be in spiritual warfare.

“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” Don't the arguments and fightings come from the lusts that war in our members? Satan knows your needs, your battles and your desires, and he will manipulate a situation or event to produce a certain outcome.

Nobody is innocent in an argument or a fight; it takes two to engage. There's an aggressor and a receiver of the aggression, and how you reply to it dictates how the warfare goes.

precepts.why:
“Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth”: kill your members upon the earth. “fornication”: that's the lust within you. You might argue because you're not getting enough, not engaging sexually with your spouse; so sometimes you fornicate, sometimes you watch porn. Something in you is causing contention in the marriage. “uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence”: evil sexual desires. “and covetousness, which is idolatry”.

Your members go into the sins, and it doesn't always have to be sexual. It could be anger, whatever you're dealing with. Whatever demons and spirits you have internally are why you have arguments and fight amongst yourselves.

You have to identify the triggers in a relationship that disrupt your marriage. What is in you that you haven't realized, paid attention to, identified and documented, that keeps the marriage contentious, digressive and stagnant instead of progressive?

sense.text:
Arguments don't happen out of thin air. They are a choice: the person who started it decided to act on it, or the receiver of aggression decided to engage the enticement. Some are legitimate, but the outcome depends on both parties engaging tactfully to keep the peace.

“Endeavouring”: fight, because there will be interruptions to the peace you are trying to form. Nobody gets married or wakes up wanting to argue, unless you're downright evil or have unresolved trauma. To fight you have to know what you're fighting and know yourself: what interferes inside you, what was whispered in your thoughts that made you agree with it, act on it and bring it to your spouse to interrupt your peace. God called us to peace, not to contention and argument.

“to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” In any tactical exchange, the first thing to keep in mind is that the husband is the head and the final authority. When a woman approaches her husband, it is tactical engagement. It is never just a thought or an idea: is it legitimate, or a thought planted in you, the enemy infiltrating your thoughts to start an argument? Did he just come home from work? Did Satan know he had a hard day, that he's struggling? The discretion of a woman fattens a man's bones: when you approach a husband, know the character of a man and of the head of a household.

“For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. The husband is the head and final authority. Sisters, when you approach him with your concerns, emotions or feelings, these are the outcomes that can come with the character of a head and an authority figure if you don't engage tactically:

Defensiveness. A desire for preeminence: he is supposed to keep the preeminence in the household, so what you bring can look like a challenge. Perceiving disagreement as a challenge to his authority as a man. Rejection of your advice: you say we should go this way, and it's rejected. A lack of communication, or withdrawal from the conversation. Questioning your approach: I don't like how you approached me. Pride and stubbornness: men, we're prideful, we're stubborn, that's how we are. A desire to control the outcome. Resistance to compromise.

Delay of decision: you want a decision now and he says, not right now. Then you argue, or act on your own outside his guidance, and that's another argument. Avoidance. Retaliation, if he's evil. Feeling undermined or disrespected by your approach. Dismissing your concerns. Selective listening: some sisters talk too much and never get to the point. Don't go to the left or the right; straight and narrow. You've got five seconds to get your point across: I don't want a book, I want a sentence. Refusing to revisit previous decisions: I decide when I want to decide. Anger and frustration. Difficulty acknowledging his wife's feelings.

Rules of engagement, sisters: your approach is everything, and timing is everything. Expect these outcomes and learn to receive them, instead of asking why is this happening and arguing because you don't like it. Assess the situation, be spiritual and discern. It is warfare, because your response can turn into arguments and fighting, and a power struggle is a lust within you.

Brothers, we complain about our wives: why is she like this, why does she do this? Understanding your wife, the nature of a woman and how she was created, also decides the outcome of the conversation. She is the weaker vessel, and certain characteristics come with the weaker vessel. You might be angry at the response, but it's because of how she was created; you can't get angry, you have to learn to work within her creation.

“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge”: deal with your wife according to the scriptures, not by your personal emotions or feelings. There's an evil way and a right way to deal with her. We can all look back and say, maybe I shouldn't have done that: you know her triggers just as she knows yours, and sometimes you say something out of spite, on purpose, because that's the outcome you wanted.

“giving honour unto the wife”. If you look at your wife and see every flaw, how can you be happy? Understand how she's created, deal within that creation, and deal with her tactfully according to knowledge. As husband and head you have the spiritual ability and the scriptures to order her mind, to structure, organize, teach and guide her.

“as unto the weaker vessel”. These are the outcomes to expect when you engage with your wife: she gets emotional; she is very wordy, and the conversation goes in many directions; emotionally disengaged; self-centered, all about her; easily offended, why did you correct me; difficulty controlling her emotions, she starts crying at anything; she takes correction personally: he hates me, he doesn't love me, he said he doesn't like what I'm wearing. She dwells on past disagreements, because a woman can't let go of the past; she brings up unrelated issues, makes assumptions without clarification, interrupts, talks over you, shuts down emotionally.

She withdraws affection during disagreements: sleeps in another room, or lies there like a mummy, no spirit, no love, plain as a sandwich with no seasoning on the chicken. And she expects you to read her mind: walking around the house angry, coffee with no sugar in it, what's wrong, nothing. I'm angry because you didn't read my thoughts. Well, I'm not God; we're not Professor X. That's the expected outcome when you engage in this tactical warfare.

The reasons we fight and argue in marriage. Number one: pride and the need to be right. Everybody wants to be right, the man as well as the woman.

“Only by pride cometh contention”: by two parties' inability to take correction or hear one another. One gives the correction, one receives it, and somebody has the pride not to apply the scriptures, receive the correction or take the advice. Because of that pride comes contention, strife, malice, hatred and disagreement.

“but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well-advised one says: I might be right, but to endeavour to keep the peace I'll suffer wrongfully and let the Lord intervene, just as the Lord intervened on Sarah's behalf with Abraham. It might not happen this time, but I'll be patient and let the Lord reveal whether I'm right or wrong, and take the correction. Somebody has to be right and somebody has to be wrong to keep the peace. Pride and the need to be right is a reason there's no peace in a marriage.

Number two: feeling disrespected and unappreciated. Everybody wants their position and role understood. The husband wants to be acknowledged and appreciated for providing: daddy pays the light bill so the lights are on, pays for gas and oil so there's heat. Sometimes, women, you take it for granted, as if it happens by osmosis, and don't give reverence: thank you for the lights, the heat, the roof over my head. The woman likewise wants her role acknowledged: I see you taking care of the kids, cooking, keeping the house clean; I understand you had a hard day.

“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself”: love her, her position and her role in the marriage, just as you love yourself. “and the wife see that she reverence her husband”: reverence his position and role, not with disrespect, both appreciating what the other brings to the table. Everybody wants a compliment every so often; it keeps us going.

How do sisters show appreciation? Sex, food, love, care, all of it, and train your kids to show it too. Sisters want to be told they look nice, a kiss, constant affirmation; it shows their value. The woman was made to please the man, and when you acknowledge that she's pleasing you, it gives her a sense of purpose, pride and joy, because she's fulfilling the reason she was born.

Number three: poor communication and failure to listen. “let every man be swift to hear”: in communication both parties have to listen to each other. Sisters, remember the rules of engagement: to get your message across, use fewer words, be intentional and direct.

“slow to speak”: sometimes you have a response ready before you've even heard. Let it settle: let me hear the concern and meditate on it, because my response could trigger an argument. Meditate on your response; it could be a thought placed in you to ignite the argument. Observe your words: is this profitable, is it beneficial?

“slow to wrath”: God called us to peace. There shouldn't be contention, argument, strife and malice in a relationship; the scripture says to enjoy the wife of thy youth.

Number four: financial disagreement. “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness”: the husband, as the head, tends to plenteousness. What do I have in reserve? Balance the finances, save for a rainy day, for a bad situation. Preserving his household should be every man's objective and goal.

“but of every one that is hasty only to want.” The one who says I want this now, I want that, comes to lack. The husband has one way of thinking about money and the wife another: you never give me anything, I don't have any clothes. That causes contention, so there has to be communication about money: saving, and balance with the woman's needs. Women like fashion; they want to look nice, to go out and be taken out. One brother couldn't figure out his wife's issue until he gave her money to get her nails done, and she's been happy ever since. Whatever works, works. Communication is key.

Number five: lack of self-control and anger. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” You must have rule over your own spirit: control your emotions, your anger and your mouth.

Both husband and wife have to understand that the things we say can break each other. Women know what to say to break a man and exactly how to trigger him, and a man knows what to say to a woman.

Number six: unresolved resentment and bitterness. “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice”. Put away the past and the trauma, the things from five conversations ago, ten moons ago, three atonements ago. Put the bitterness and the grudge away from the future of your relationship.

Sisters, learn to let things go. Bringing up a past situation in an argument shows you never grew from it: you were holding on to it, waiting to bring it up, and that is why you never showed love and affection or became your best version for your husband.
“And be ye kind one to another”. We have to learn to be kind one to another.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” The husband may feel he carries the financial responsibility and want his wife to understand it; the wife may feel overwhelmed with the children and the household. Don't look only at what you are carrying.

Look at what she's been going through: with the kids all day, every day, from sun up to sun down, cleaning. That can break her, and these things happen; there was the Edomite demon that killed her three kids. You come home and her eyes are bloodshot. Kids will drive you crazy; try it one day and everybody ends up in a headlock and sent to their rooms. It is psychologically traumatizing if you don't give her the space to stabilize, think, and meditate on the scripture. Give her peace and rest so she can regroup and be her best for you. People can't run like machines continually, and then you say she doesn't reverence me or care for me, when you never gave her the opportunity.

Sisters, think on your husband's things too. He's tired, financially tired: work, bills, the things he deals with in the world. Men don't talk much about their feelings or what they go through psychologically, the burden of a man in society to provide and keep the household running. Understand that, approach him and treat him as the head, and be kindly affectionate one to another.

Number eight: a lack of affection and emotional connection. “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.” Both spouses need affection, companionship and emotional connection, whatever you think or say. King Solomon said to be always ravished with her love. A lack of sex in a relationship causes contention: why is he angry? He never got a release. Why is she angry? The water's backed up.

That is the art of war: understanding the tactical warfare and the fight we're in. There are rules of engagement in every aspect and direction of life, every thought process, every second, minute, hour and day: the thoughts that filter through your mind, what somebody says and why, whether it was intentional, what response it is trying to trigger in you, how Satan is moving and what he is planning for the future. Write it down, brothers and sisters. Study it, acknowledge it, and fight.
